RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. In laboratory medicine and hospital management, women are heavily represented, so a four-woman panel is statistically unremarkable — it is a byproduct of who holds senior roles, not evidence of bias. Raising it as your opening argument will read as a grievance and damage your credibility on the points that actually matter.

Those points are stronger: a PhD and eight years of section leadership versus a master's and a management course is a real qualifications gap, and "broad leadership experience" is vague enough to deserve specifics. Missing your written explanation after two weeks may also breach your employer's or jurisdiction's duty to give reasons.

Chase the written reasons, in writing. Judge the decision once you see them.
